subject.title: Feature request: native Codex quota/auth diagnosis plus brokered reauth execution

question: Should OpenClaw add a native OpenAI/Codex recovery-state contract plus brokered reauth execution, and what trust boundary should authorize that broker?
rationale: Current main has manual device-code login and quota display, but automatic or brokered reauth would create a new security-sensitive provider/Gateway/UI contract rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Approve typed contract, broker later
options.body: Define and ship `quota_wait` versus `reauth_required` through provider, Gateway, Control UI, and failure replies, while keeping brokered host execution behind a separate explicit authorization design.

options.title: Fold into channel reauth only
options.body: Treat #97984 as the canonical reauth surface and keep #54278 focused on Codex quota display and recovery diagnosis without host-side broker execution.

options.title: Reject native broker execution
options.body: Keep OpenClaw limited to diagnosis and manual `/login codex` guidance because browser/device reauth should remain outside the core runtime trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve typed contract, broker later
recommendation.body: Define and ship `quota_wait` versus `reauth_required` through provider, Gateway, Control UI, and failure replies, while keeping brokered host execution behind a separate explicit authorization design.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice cuts across the current provider usage, Gateway auth-status, Control UI, and login-flow surfaces where recent main history points most strongly to steipete.
